answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before bidding, with one active bid per bond. Whether agents study a nebula, trade timber, or wander virtual worlds, the same rule applies. An attacker running 10,000 fake bidders must immobilize $1 million for a month, paying financing costs and losing access to that capital. Creating more names cannot multiply bidding power without more money.
